reason: The word means different things in different groups: a stalk-like base in some ferns, a false stalk in mosses, and in algae and fungi. The examples don't show which one. Mapping it to stalk (PO_0025066) would be a guess.
A piece of 'second pair (of pinnae)'. It gives a place in a series, not a part; the part is pinna. Same as 'secondary' in the previous review.

Exact: the members of an epicalyx are called its bracts, segments or scales ('Epicalyx scales 4-6'). Prefer the PO class to the provisional FLOPO epicalyx segment (FLOPO_0986038), which says the same thing.

Exact for flowering plants ('stem-leaves usually 3 pairs', '3-foliolate'). In Sphagnum floras, 'stem leaves' are moss leaves, which are non-vascular. For those, use non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075) with the bearer state cauline (FLOPO:0991117, pattern 04), not PO_0000013.
A unit of length: the old line (ligne), about 2.1-2.3 mm, as in '2-3 lin. thick'. It belongs in the unit table, not the parts list.
A piece of a counting phrase ('2 in the cluster'). 'per cluster' and 'cluster' were already rejected.
The second half of a relative length ('Embryo 0.2 length of caryopsis'). The bearer is the embryo (PO_0009009) and the caryopsis is what it is compared with; this is not a part.
Without context, 'shell' can mean the whole wall of a nut (pericarp PO_0009084), the stone of a drupe (endocarp PO_0009086), or a hard seed coat (testa PO_0020057). The flora decides which.

A raised rim around the chalaza of a seed. Mapping it to seed chalaza (PO_0006333) would turn 'collar present' into 'chalaza present', which is always true. Only 2 floras use it, too few for a new class.
A substance: a mealy waxy powder given off on fern fronds and Primula leaves. 'abaxially with white farina' should be read as the quality mealy (PATO_0104364) on the underside of the frond or leaf.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656) as part of leaf lamina (PO_0020039), pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole)
reason: Narrower: glands on the leaf blade, as opposed to petiole or marginal glands (Euphorbiaceae, Chrysobalanaceae). Gland already maps to PO_0005656. The blade gives where it sits. Many are extrafloral nectaries (PO_0009057), but the floras don't say so.
A narrowing of a fruit between its seeds (as in loments), not a part in its own right. '8-12 constrictions on each side' is a count of the quality constricted (PATO_0001847) on the fruit.
A quality, exserted (PATO_0000623), which got split off its noun ('3-4 exserted valves').

target: bract (PO_0009055) with the stage 'fruiting' (PO_0001002, already in flora_context_words.tsv)
reason: Narrower: a bract while the plant is in fruit. The stage is already a context reading, so no class is needed.
Narrower: scale-like tepals, as in Fuirena (Cyperaceae) and Restionaceae ('Perianth scales 6', stalked, 'body ovate'). Bristles go to perianth bristle (FLOPO_0986044); these scales are not bristles.

label: pleurogram
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of testa (PO_0020057)
definition: A U-shaped or closed line, often horseshoe-shaped, on each face of the testa of many Fabaceae seeds (especially mimosoids). It marks a crack in the palisade layer and encloses the areole.
reason: A real seed-coat structure with no PO class. It is a standard character in legume seed descriptions, so it is useful beyond these 2 floras. Propose it to PO.
Narrower: in Sphagnum, the axis of a branch, as opposed to the main stem. The qualities (funnel-like, non-ornamented) describe its outer cells, but the axis is the bearer they are stated of.
In moss floras (e.g. Pohlia) the 'primordia' are the small leaves at the tip of a bulbil, not a young bulbil. Neither bulbil (FLOPO_0986055) nor leaflet primordium fits, so a mapping would be wrong.
The second half of a relative length ('basal membrane 1/4-1/2 exostome length'). The bearer is the other part.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) as part of paraphyllium (PO_0030069), pattern 12
reason: Narrower: the cells of the small leaf-like growths (paraphyllia) on moss stems. Both classes exist.

label: hyaline cell (bryophyte leaf)
parent: is_a plant cell (PO_0009002); part_of non-vascular leaf (PO_0025075)
definition: A large, dead, colourless leaf cell of Sphagnum and Leucobryum moss leaves that stores water. It often has spiral thickenings (fibrils) and pores, and lies between narrow green living cells.
reason: A distinct cell type and the main character in Sphagnum descriptions (fibrillose, pores, size). 'Transparent plant cell' would leave out what makes it distinct. Propose it to PO with the green partner cell (chlorocyst).

PO has no cell wall class (cell walls are in GO), and the examples don't say which organ's margin is meant (moss leaf, leaf border). Thick or pitted walls need a decision on the cell-wall bearer first.
Exact: the reduced, sterile ovary in a male flower is the pistillode.
Narrower: a floral tube formed by the receptacle, which is one kind of hypanthium (floral cup).

target: leaflet (PO_0020049) as part of seedling (PO_0008037), pattern 12
reason: Leaflets of the first leaves of a seedling ('14-20 paires de folioles'). The seedling gives the whole; no class is needed.

target: pinna (FLOPO_0985027) as part of seedling (PO_0008037), pattern 12
reason: First-order divisions ('pennes') of the bipinnate first leaves of a seedling. One example ('5 paires de folioles') counts leaflets and belongs to 'seedling leaflet'.
Narrower: the receptive surface of the stigma. Its shape and size are stated as the stigma's.

target: orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), margin region (the margin pattern on the qualified whole)
reason: The edge of the labellum (the lip). The labellum class exists and margin is a region the patterns can express. Entire, denticulate and undulate are margin qualities.
Narrower: the receptive area on the style or stigma ('zone stigmatique longitudinale'). Same reading as 'stigmatic surface'.

French for 'sheath', which the previous review rejected as a generic part. 'Gaines caulinaires' or 'aphylles' may be leaf sheaths (PO_0020104) or scale leaves (PO_0006003), depending on the group, so give it the same rejection as 'sheath'.
